tasks.task: Plan a fundraising appeal campaign

items.when: When the client sets an appeal date, to run the cycle from story to thank-yous
When you have one consented story and real cost figures and need the whole appeal
When you have donor groups and giving history, to set gift amounts and a schedule
When all you have is a gift export, to group donors by how recently and often they gave

tasks.task: Write an appeal letter or email

items.when: Before writing, to shape the story with checked facts, consent and a way to withdraw
When you need one appeal as a letter, an email or both, with two openings to test
When the appeal goes by email, to get three different personal drafts of the story
When the email needs subject lines in several angles to choose from
When it goes by post, to review the envelope line, the ask, the letter and the look
When the draft leans on guilt or urgency, to see which levers are true
When the letter talks about the charity and should start from what the reader cares about

tasks.task: Write a donation page

items.when: When the giving page needs real gift amounts, checked claims and a repeat-gift choice
When the top of the page is flat, to get five headlines with a subhead and button
When the page is drafted, to rank what would stop a visitor giving
Before launch, to check every impact claim against the group's own records

tasks.task: Write thank-yous for each donor group

items.when: When one generic thank-you should become a short set for each kind of donor
When the thank-you must carry the right legal acknowledgment wording
When one donor deserves a personal note with one specific, true appreciation
When you must plan who gets thanked how, and when the next message follows

tasks.task: Check receipts, acknowledgments and Gift Aid wording

items.when: Before a gala, auction or year-end mailing, to check wording against official guidance
When the wording fails the check and needs rewriting by gift type
When gifts are goods or auction items and need acceptance rules and receipt wording

tasks.task: Plan donor care until the next ask

items.when: When the client can give twenty minutes a week and wants a monthly review
When donor records need clear stages, next steps, owners and review dates
When lapsed donors need a plan to renew and new donors need a welcome
When first-time donors should get a short welcome series by email
When you want to ask supporters why they give and what they want to hear

tasks.task: Write a supporter newsletter or impact update

items.when: When the newsletter needs sections, reader groups and a schedule between appeals
When you have supporter questions and news and need the issue drafted
When the issue carries a story about a person the group helped
When the issue needs subject lines in several angles
Before sending, to get cuts and a ship or fix verdict

tasks.task: Write an impact story or annual report

items.when: When a yearly report needs a plan and every fact, number and name checked
When the report needs stories that respect each person and have clear consent
When the numbers are thin, to set what to measure and the rules for reporting it
When the report lists outputs and needs one true incident that shows the change

tasks.task: Plan a fundraising event pack

items.when: When you need the event budget, income scenarios, auction tracker and day schedule
When the event needs sponsor tiers, pitch copy and a list of promises to keep
Before the event, to check ticket, auction and donation receipts are worded right
After the event, to follow up each guest by what they asked or pledged

tasks.task: Plan a team or peer-to-peer fundraiser

items.when: When supporters raise money in teams and captains need tools and tracking
When fundraisers and their sponsors each need their own thank-you
When the team fundraiser is part of a wider appeal and must share its story and costs

tasks.task: Find and rank funders worth a bid

items.when: When you need trusts, foundations, lottery and council funders ranked by real fit
When you have the programme, place and need and want a shortlist with grant dates
When a funder looks promising, for a go or no-go call before any writing
When one funder matters, to build a sourced file on what it funds and who decides

tasks.task: Check eligibility against a funder's guidelines

items.when: Before writing any bid, to test every rule in the guidelines against your facts
When the guidelines are long, to sort requirements into must-haves and score the fit

tasks.task: Build a 12-month funding calendar

items.when: Once a year for the full review, then monthly to keep the calendar current
When ranked funders need deadlines, amounts and prep time on one calendar

tasks.task: Write a grant application

items.when: When the funder is chosen and each question needs an answer from the group's facts
When you have funder rules, programme facts and budget and need the required sections
When the funder wants a letter of inquiry first, with a list of claims to prove
When answers are over the word limit or full of sector jargon
Before submitting, to face the hardest questions an assessor would ask

tasks.task: Write the needs statement, outcomes and measures

items.when: When the need is asserted, not shown, to plan the research and map other providers
When the bid needs a clear map from activities to outcomes, with assumptions
When the funder asks how you will measure, to set measures, dates and owners
When the statement cites statistics, to check each against sources and note conflicts

tasks.task: Build the budget table and budget narrative

items.when: When the application needs a budget table that matches the answers
When shared costs must be split fairly across programmes before you cost the bid
When the budget is drafted, to check it against what the funder will and will not pay for

tasks.task: Write a progress or final report to a funder

items.when: When a report is due, to turn your records into an honest report in the funder's template
When the report needs spending reconciled to the grant, with gaps named
When the spending table is drafted and needs its evidence checked line by line
When spending differs from the budget and the funder needs a plain reason

tasks.task: Track restricted grant money against free cash

items.when: When you must split bank cash into restricted grant money and money free to spend
When a new person takes over a restricted fund and needs its rules and records

tasks.task: Plan cultivation for top prospects

items.when: When loyal supporters could give more, using only your records and what they shared
When each prospect needs a stage, a next step, an owner and a review date
When the goal is large, to test it with a gift table built on real prospects

tasks.task: Prepare an ask meeting with a prep sheet and script

items.when: When a prospect is ready and you need the prep sheet, the ask and the follow-up
Before the meeting, to plan a warm start and questions the donor enjoys answering
When the ask feels hard, to plan to listen first, say it once and agree a next step
After the meeting, to keep a one-page card of facts, promises and the next contact
When the script is all about the charity's need and not the donor's interests

tasks.task: Write a corporate partnership or sponsorship proposal

items.when: When you need tiers, benefits and pitch copy a company can say yes to
When you want several partnership ideas before choosing what to propose
When the company asked for a written proposal with value, cost, timeline and proof
When the proposal is drafted, to read it as the sponsor would weigh cost and fit

tasks.task: Brief on companies and trusts you could approach

items.when: When you need a sourced file on a company or trust before you approach it
When a one-page summary of a company's finances and business is enough
When the brief is about a person, to keep to your own records and what they shared

tasks.task: Set the fundraising plan and report to the board

items.when: When the group needs a few funded priorities chosen from real evidence
When grants and gifts are not enough, to test income ideas with break-even sums
When staff and board need clear fundraising measures, owners and actions
When the board must decide something and needs results, risks and next steps

always.when: When an appeal, bid or report states a number or result you cannot trace to the records
Before anything goes to a donor or funder, to fix lines that sound machine-written
Before sending, to catch typos and funder, donor and project names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When a funder wants an evaluation plan or evidence of outcomes beyond simple counts
When restricted fund spending must be traced in the books before a report
When a gala or community event needs a venue, suppliers and a run sheet
When the appeal runs as an email series with segments and inbox checks
When corporate sponsorship is a programme of its own with renewals and reporting
When the appeal, report or event needs layout and print files

gaps: No library item writes a fundraising appeal letter; only the kit prompt and skill do
No library item checks a funder's eligibility rules line by line, or scores a draft answer against scoring criteria
No library item builds a grant budget table with a narrative, or checks that the two match
No library item writes a funder progress or final report from programme records
No library item plans major gift cultivation or writes an ask script; only the kit skill does
No library item covers Gift Aid, tax receipts or acknowledgment wording by country
No library item plans a regular giving or monthly giving programme, or a legacy giving ask
No library item gives clearly different versions of a grant answer or a thank-you to compare
No library item builds a logic model or theory of change in a funder's format
No library item analyses donor data for retention, upgrade and lapse rates
